answer: Walnut Rotation Quotas: each epoch a public randomness beacon picks a vertex in a registration graph and a walnut threshold, assigning identities to shards by hashed draw. An identity may hold at most one seat per shard, and seats are revealed only after commit, so an attacker cannot precompute placement. Excess identities land on a knoll shard excluded from rewards and work, forcing attackers to overbuild registration capacity per usable seat.
